name: Philips Hue Smart Plug (US)

radios.note: Bluetooth for direct app control; Zigbee to the Hue Bridge.

matter.note: No Matter certification found for the plug itself. Hue says Bridge-connected products are exposed to Matter by the Bridge, and Bluetooth-only setups cannot use Matter.

apple_home.note: The product page lists Apple Home among assistants that need a Hue Bridge.

google_home.note: The product page lists Google Assistant among assistants that need a Hue Bridge.

alexa.note: The product page lists Alexa among assistants that need a Hue Bridge.

smartthings.note: The Hue Bridge page lists Samsung SmartThings compatibility.

home_assistant.note: Official Hue integration controls devices connected to a Hue Bridge. Users report plugs show up as light entities.

hubRequired.note: Basic control works over Bluetooth from the Hue app; the Hue Bridge is needed for voice assistants, ecosystems and remote access.

localControl.note: Bluetooth control without a bridge; the Hue Bridge also offers a local API used by Home Assistant.

energyMonitoring.note: Hue's pages describe on/off switching only and list no metering, but none says explicitly that it is absent.

maxLoadWatts.note: Hue support gives 1800 W for North America (100–120 V).

summary: The US Philips Hue Smart Plug is an on/off plug for 100–120 V outlets, rated 1800 W. It can be controlled over Bluetooth from the Hue app, but Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa, SmartThings and Home Assistant all need a Hue Bridge. With the Bridge it also reaches Matter platforms.
caveats: Home Assistant users report the plug appears as a light, so it can respond to 'all lights off' commands.
